ui_bugs.issue: STILL WHITE-ON-WHITE in BOTH light and dark. Computed style: backgroundColor rgb(255,255,255) AND color rgb(255,255,255). Screenshot (iter291_landing_cta_light2.jpeg) confirms an empty white pill with no visible label on the teal section. The iter290 fix (narrowing .force-white to :not([class*='bg-']) at /app/frontend/src/index.css:279-286) is IRRELEVANT for this button because the actual override comes from a DIFFERENT rule: /app/frontend/src/index.css:1013-1017 sets `.bg-primary-k a { color: #FFFFFF !important; text-decoration: none !important; }` — the button is a <Link> (renders as <a>) nested inside <section className='bg-primary-k'> (Landing.jsx:526). This teal-surface link-color rule wins over .text-primary-k regardless of the .force-white narrowing. Fix options: (a) at /app/frontend/src/index.css:1013 narrow selector to `.bg-primary-k a:not([class*='bg-white']):not(.text-teal-solid)`; (b) at /app/frontend/src/pages/Landing.jsx:533 add inline style={{color:'#0E4D52'}} OR replace text-primary-k with an inline-styled span child that carries the teal color; (c) introduce a semantic utility class .text-on-white with `color:#0E4D52 !important` and add it to this button.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix final-cta-signup white-on-white. Root cause is /app/frontend/src/index.css:1013-1017 — `.bg-primary-k a { color:#FFFFFF !important; }` overrides the button's `text-primary-k` class because the button is a <Link> (renders <a>) inside <section className='bg-primary-k'>. The iter290 change to .force-white did NOT touch this rule. Recommended fix: narrow /app/frontend/src/index.css:1013 selector to `.bg-primary-k a:not([class*='bg-white']):not([class*='bg-surface'])` so white-backgrounded CTAs on teal keep their own dark label. Alternatively, at /app/frontend/src/pages/Landing.jsx:533 add `style={{color:'#0E4D52'}}` (inline wins over the !important cascade if declared on the element itself with the same specificity — safer is to introduce a `.text-teal-solid { color:#0E4D52 !important }` utility and include it in the button).

MEDIUM: Confirm /app/statements list surfaces a link/row to individual statement detail — could not re-exercise statement-download-original-btn / statement-audit-log-link / statement-archive-btn / statement-permanent-delete-btn / statement-restore-btn this iter because only /upload and /archived index pages were reachable from the list. iter290 verified these on a live detail URL, so this is not necessarily a regression.

MEDIUM: Family Wall — /app/family renders the Family Thread chat, not the wall-post-* card grid. Please confirm the correct route for the FamilyWall component OR update the review spec route. Zero wall-post-* testIDs found under /app/family.
critical_code_review_comments: index.css has TWO layers of aggressive text-force-white — (a) .force-white at line 279 (now narrowed to :not([class*='bg-']) ) and (b) the teal-surface link rule at line 1013 (.bg-primary-k a → color:#FFFFFF !important). They shadow each other. The iter290 narrowing solved the .force-white case but the second layer still catches the final-cta-signup Link. Recommend consolidating into a single `.force-white`/`[data-teal-surface]` mechanism with a shared :not([class*='bg-white']) exception applied consistently across `p, span, li, h*, a` selectors.

rca of the issue: final-cta-signup white-on-white: <Link to='/signup' className='bg-white text-primary-k ...'> at /app/frontend/src/pages/Landing.jsx:533 is a descendant of <section className='bg-primary-k'> at line 526. /app/frontend/src/index.css:1013-1017 declares `.bg-primary-k a, .bg-kindred-primary a, ... { color:#FFFFFF !important; }` — this !important rule beats the button's own `.text-primary-k` (color: var(--kindred-primary), non-important) so the label collapses to white on the white pill. The iter290 .force-white narrowing does NOT solve this because the guilty rule targets `a` inside `.bg-primary-k`, not `.text-primary-k` inside `.force-white`. Fix at index.css:1013 with a `:not([class*='bg-white'])` exemption, or override at the call site with an inline color.
